attributes.description: Alerts when Web Analytics page view volume drops by more than 50% in the most recent 15 minutes compared to the preceding 15 minutes, per project. Complements the server-side request-rate-drop rule with a client-side/user-facing engagement view.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Page view rate drop

investigation_guide.blob:
## Page View Rate Drop

### Triage Steps
1. Confirm the drop with the Web Analytics dashboard, filtered to the affected `vercel.project.id`.
2. Check whether the `@vercel/analytics` client SDK is still loading correctly — a bad deployment can silently strip the tracking script (this would show as a pageview drop with no corresponding server-side request drop).
3. Cross-check the server-side request-rate-drop rule — if both fired together, the issue is likely upstream (DNS, CDN, outage) rather than analytics-specific.
4. If only page views dropped (server requests look normal), suspect an ad-blocker-adjacent change, a Content-Security-Policy regression blocking the analytics script, or a consent-management change preventing the SDK from firing.

### Note
Web Analytics events are recorded client-side after page load, so this signal reflects real user-facing impact more directly than server request counts, but it is also more susceptible to browser/extension blocking as an unrelated confound.

### Escalation
If the drop is corroborated by the request-rate-drop rule or persists beyond one hour, escalate to the on-call engineer.

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.analytics.v2.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
    AND vercel.analytics.event.type == "pageview"
// Split the window in half: "recent" (last 15m) vs "baseline" (previous 15m) to detect a drop within a single evaluation
| EVAL is_recent = CASE(@timestamp >= NOW() - 15 minutes, 1, 0)
| STATS
    recent = SUM(is_recent),
    baseline = SUM(1 - is_recent)
  BY vercel.project.id
// Minimum baseline volume to avoid flagging naturally quiet/low-traffic projects
| WHERE baseline > 5
| EVAL drop_pct = ROUND(100.0 - (TO_DOUBLE(recent) / baseline * 100.0), 2)
// Alert threshold: tune based on expected traffic variance for your project
| WHERE drop_pct > 50.0
| SORT drop_pct DESC
| LIMIT 20
